THE BRIEF

The repair location is only one part of a retail maintenance job. We also confirm who approves the work, how materials arrive and which trading routes remain open. This keeps a defined tenancy repair separate from a wider centre-maintenance or make-good scope.

✺

PROPERTY IN USE

The details customers use every day

  • Shopfront and entry

    We review door hardware, tracks, fixed fittings, signs and finishes around the entrance. Operation, visibility and surface matching are considered together.

  • Inside the tenancy

    Wall and ceiling damage, lighting faults and fixed joinery are listed by position. Repairs following a water issue include a separate check of the source and affected finish.

  • Shared presentation

    Agreed directories, common-area fittings, external surfaces and access points are scoped with centre management and the relevant work boundaries.

PROPERTY IN USE

Plan the route into the work

  1. 01

    Confirm approvals and boundaries

    We identify the nominated operator or manager, the approved work area and any conditions affecting the tenancy or common space.

  2. 02

    Arrange delivery and protection

    Loading access, lifts, material dimensions, stock protection, temporary separation and waste routes are included where relevant.

  3. 03

    Sequence the finish work

    Connected repairs are completed in the agreed order, with drying or curing conditions reflected in the return-to-use plan.

PROPERTY IN USE

Check the part and the approved artwork

For signage, we confirm the text, artwork, dimensions, position and existing support before manufacturing or replacement is included in the scope. Retaining a frame and replacing a face is a different task from a complete new installation.

For visible repairs, existing profiles, finishes, paint colours and hardware models help establish a consistent result. Where an exact match is unavailable, we identify the affected area and proposed finish extent before work.

PROPERTY IN USE

Prepare a useful retail brief

  • Identify the space

    Include the tenancy or area, photographs, the defect history and the contact responsible for approvals.

  • Identify the constraints

    Tell us about trading, centre access, deliveries, retained displays and any date tied to a handover or reopening.

PROPERTY IN USE

Hand back the agreed items

We record completed items by tenancy or common area, check the operation or finish included in the scope and list remaining parts or decisions. For make-good work, completion is matched to the agreed itemised brief.

Confirm centre approval, stock protection, customer paths, loading dock and goods lift access. Establish when noisy work or temporary closures are possible.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can signs and interior defects be grouped together?+

Yes. We can develop one agreed list with separate items for sign content, fabrication or installation, and the building repairs. Access and trade sequencing are then coordinated around that list.

Can you price from a landlord’s make-good list?+

We use the list with the tenancy condition and retained items to define the work. Any unclear finish, removal or service requirement is identified before the final scope is agreed.

Who should approve work at the shopfront?+

Confirm with the tenant and centre manager who controls the affected surface, access route and work hours before the quote is settled.
